general_questions: What is your minimum size, and what fees would apply at $5M?
Can you accept grants, recoverable grants and loans into the same vehicle? If not, what structure do you suggest for the loans?
Can you lend to funds and borrowers outside the US? Any country or currency limits?
Do you have experience with subordinated debt?
Who sits on the credit committee, and what formal role can AEF have?
How deep is your underwriting, and can a separate advisor do it instead?
Can the vehicle grow later or be spun out?

organizations.name: Total Impact Capital
organizations.summary: Its Total Impact Notes are five-year notes paying 5% a year that pool loans to fund managers. The first issuance raised $3M (ImpactAlpha, Nov 3, 2025). Borrowers are fund managers focused on Latin America and the Caribbean (LocFund, NESsT's Lirio Fund, Elu Women's Empowerment Fund), plus Nithio in Africa; NESsT Lirio Fund is already in the directory.
open_questions: Could the pilot sit inside the existing Total Impact Notes, or would it be a separate series or vehicle?
How would AEF's money be separated from other noteholders, and how much say would AEF have over borrowers?
Can the Notes accept grants or recoverable grants as well as investor purchases?

sources.label: ImpactAlpha, Total Impact Notes first issuance (Nov 3, 2025)

per_aef: Small enough that it might run the pilot through the existing Notes program rather than a separate vehicle.

organizations.name: ImpactAssets
organizations.lends_internationally_note: via DAF investments, e.g. an emerging-markets credit strategy
organizations.underwriting: Client (AEF or its advisor) for client-recommended investments; ImpactAssets does a compliance-level review
organizations.summary: The DAF lets donors recommend impact investments in funds and companies as well as grants. It supports international grants and expenditure responsibility grants. Several services appear to be open to non-DAF clients: a PRI account for foundations, Pooled Donor Funds, Supporting Organizations ($10M+ accounts), custom portfolios, due diligence and back-office administration. The DAF can make loans through the Client Recommended Investment service, with ImpactAssets handling execution, servicing, monitoring and reporting. For client-recommended investments, the client sources the deal and does the due diligence; ImpactAssets reviews impact commitments, runs basic AML, IRS-compliance and fraud checks, acts as legal investor and fiduciary, and can decline. An emerging-markets credit strategy is available through the DAF.
open_questions: Are PRI accounts, Pooled Donor Funds, custom portfolios, due diligence and back-office administration available without an ImpactAssets DAF?
What is the minimum for a client-recommended loan, and what fees apply to a $5M account?
Could a separate entity accept outside loans alongside an AEF DAF?

ImpactAssets, "Investing Close to Home to Build Intergenerational Wealth"

organizations.name: Innpact
organizations.type: Impact fund structuring firm and third-party AIFM (Luxembourg)
organizations.accepts_loans_in_note: Not described. Its funds are Luxembourg regulated vehicles (RAIF/SIF) built for investor commitments; grant or recoverable-grant inflows are not described
organizations.lends_internationally_note: e.g. the ABC Fund, a private debt fund with a global mandate focused on Sub-Saharan Africa (S30)
organizations.underwriting: Not done by Innpact as AIFM in the ABC example; ABC's investment advisor is Investisseurs & Partenaires (I&P) (S30).
organizations.summary: Luxembourg impact finance firm that sets up and manages impact funds (S29). Services include fund strategy and structuring; a third-party AIFM dedicated to impact funds, supporting RAIF and SIF vehicles and blended finance structures (S29); a Mauritius fund-management route for African funds through MIFGA, a joint initiative with AXIS (S29); and a white-label impact bond issuance platform, Imagine Impact Bonds (S29). Its agriculture work shows two distinct roles. Design only: Innpact supported IDH in the design, structuring and incorporation of the EUR 100 million IDH Farmfit Fund (Farmfit Fund B.V., Netherlands, January 2020) (S31); the fund is managed by IDH Investment Management (S32). AIFM: Innpact Fund Management S.A. has been AIFM of the Agri-Business Capital (ABC) Fund, a Luxembourg private debt fund, since 2023 (S30), and still listed it among its funds under management on 30 June 2026 (S33). See the ABC Fund example. Innpact's site gives no fund sizes or minimums (S29).
organizations.exclusion_reason: Judgment call. Luxembourg regulated fund structures and AIFM costs are likely too heavy for a permanent ~$5M vehicle, and the structure is not built for US grant and recoverable-grant inflows (per AEF / to confirm). Revisit if the pilot grows or spins out, particularly with European or DFI investors: the ABC split between a regulated AIFM and a separate investment advisor is close to the AIF model of AEF participating in decisions while a third party underwrites.
open_questions: Could Imagine Impact Bonds carry a ~$5M lending program, and can it accept US investors and US charitable capital?
What are the minimum fund size and annual costs for Innpact's AIFM services?

Does Innpact provide central administration (NAV, investor register, transfer agency), or only the AIFM role? An AIFM is not the same as a fund administrator; Innpact's pages describe the AIFM role for ABC, not administration.
Who is ABC's current investment advisor, and when did it change from Injaro?

sources.label: Innpact Fund Management S.A., PAI statement (30 June 2026)

per_aef: Not a pilot host; a candidate partner for a later, larger or spun-out vehicle.

examples.name: Olamina Fund
examples.label: Closest structure
examples.structure: Olamina Fund, LLC, offered to accredited investors under Rule 506(c). Investors choose a 5-year note at a fixed 1% a year or a 7-year note at a fixed 1.5%. The initial $40M came from two of Candide's donor-advised fund clients; ImpactAssets made the initial investments, advised by members of the Pritzker family. It makes senior unsecured loans of up to $4M to CDFIs and other loan funds, plus smaller direct loans, with at least 80% of loans going to organizations led by people of color and women. The credit committee is the Managing Director and Candide's two founding partners, and a Community Advisory Board has a veto over every loan.
examples.why_relevant: A note-issuing vehicle run by an investment manager, with a DAF as one of its investors. This gets around the fact that a DAF can't accept loans: an AEF DAF could invest in such a vehicle alongside other lenders. The community veto mirrors AEF's participatory governance.
examples.key_differences: US only (rural areas, Native lands and the deep South). Its initial $40M is eight times the pilot.

examples.name: Total Impact Notes
examples.label: Closest international operations
examples.structure: Five-year notes paying 5% a year that pool loans to fund managers, mainly in Latin America and the Caribbean (LocFund, NESsT's Lirio Fund, Elu Women's Empowerment Fund) plus Nithio in Africa. The first issuance raised $3M (November 2025).
examples.why_relevant: Does what the AIF plans to do, lending to intermediary funds outside the US, at a similar small scale.
examples.key_differences: A higher fixed investor return, and no participatory governance described.

sources.label: ImpactAlpha, Total Impact Notes first issuance (Nov 3, 2025)

examples.name: WRI TerraFund with Realize Impact
examples.label: Mission organization working through a third-party host
examples.run_by: WRI Africa, with Realize Impact as partner (the release doesn't describe Realize's specific role).
examples.structure: TerraFund is WRI Africa's financing program for restoration enterprises. It has made 39 debt and equity investments worth $5M. Barka Fund, which is in the directory, has advised TerraFund since 2021, and WRI Africa invested $4M in Barka Fund in January 2025.
examples.why_relevant: A mission organization running a ~$5M international lending program with a third-party charitable partner, close to the pilot in both scale and setup.
examples.key_differences: Invests directly in enterprises rather than in funds, and uses both debt and equity.

examples.name: Abundance Circle
examples.label: Fund of funds run as a DAF
examples.run_by: Founders Luis Javier Castro and Brian Gallagher; administered by ImpactAssets.
examples.structure: An evergreen, global fund of funds structured as a donor-advised fund and administered by ImpactAssets, anchored by a gift from the NoVo Foundation. Its philanthropic capital takes first-loss positions to draw in other investors, and returns are recycled.
examples.why_relevant: Shows the DAF-hosted fund-of-funds option already in operation.
examples.key_differences: Much larger (it aims to raise $100M in its first year). The source doesn't say whether it uses debt or equity. Its themes are deep tech, energy transition and circular economy, and community-based economic development.

examples.name: Social Finance Impact First Fund
examples.label: Mixing charitable and investment capital

structure.text: Described as a professionally managed, diversified fund of funds that provides flexible, risk-tolerant capital.
Accepts LP investments and recoverable grants from DAFs, foundations and taxable accounts. Its mechanics and terms aren't explained on the Social Finance page.
Uses a feeder fund structure to accept DAF capital through recoverable grants, so charitable and profit-seeking capital are deployed into the same investments.
Holdings include Mad Capital and Fractal Agriculture.

examples.why_relevant: It shows one way to combine charitable and investment money in a fund of funds. It isn't a host candidate. For a host-style arrangement, see Social Finance Custom Portfolio Management above.
examples.key_differences: US-focused. Offered only to accredited investors under Regulation D.

sources.label: Social Finance Impact First Fund page (hosted by NYU Law)

examples.name: Buen Vivir Fund
examples.label: Lessons learned
examples.run_by: Thousand Currents, which hosted the fund and was both its funder and facilitator. Closed in 2023.
examples.structure: A participatory fund whose members included grassroots groups from Mexico, Guatemala, India, Nepal and South Africa, along with US philanthropies. It made six loans across three countries between 2018 and 2020, each paired with grant support. Instead of interest, borrowers made "aportes", solidarity contributions above the return of principal. A Members Assembly, not an investment committee, governed the fund.
examples.why_relevant: The closest precedent in mission, geography and governance.
examples.what_happened: Pandemic-era unrestricted grants strained its financial model, and by late 2022 only one member could make an aporte. In 2023 Thousand Currents ended all programmatic investment, and all outstanding loans were converted into grants.
examples.lessons: Regulatory compliance is difficult and expensive for small funds; participation doesn't remove power dynamics, especially when the host is also the funder; not all work suits loans; and responsibility should match readiness.

examples.name: ABC Fund (Agri-Business Capital Fund)
examples.label: Regulated manager with a separate investment advisor
examples.structure: Luxembourg SA, SICAV-RAIF launched in February 2019 (S30), originally sponsored by IFAD (S34). Invests in private debt with a global mandate focused on Sub-Saharan Africa; end-beneficiaries are smallholder farmers and local communities (S30). Innpact Fund Management S.A. was selected as AIFM in 2022 and appointed toward the end of Q1 2023 (S30). ABC was originally managed by Bamboo Capital Partners (S34, S35), with Injaro Investments as investment advisor (S34). Innpact's website currently lists Investisseurs & Partenaires (I&P) as investment advisor (S30). In 2020 the fund had a target size of €200 million and had investors including IFAD (with funds from the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation), the European Commission, the Organisation of African, Caribbean and Pacific States, Luxembourg and AGRA (S35).
examples.why_relevant: Separates the regulated fund manager from the party advising on investments — close to the AIF model, where AEF takes part in decisions and a third party underwrites. Lends to agriculture in Sub-Saharan Africa and is structured to blend public with private capital (S35).
examples.key_differences: Much larger (€200 million 2020 target vs. a ~$5M pilot). A Luxembourg regulated fund with public and institutional investors; accepting US grants or recoverable grants is not described. No participatory governance described.

sources.label: Africa Global Funds, IFAD invests $9m in ABC Fund (Apr 29, 2020)
